content_metadata.description: This video demonstrates the setup and operation of a Tangent Galvanometer experiment to measure the horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field.

qAndA.answer: The instrument used is called a Tangent Galvanometer.
qAndA.question: What is the name of the instrument used to measure the horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field?

qAndA.answer: The battery eliminator is providing a voltage of 8 volts.
qAndA.question: What voltage is being provided by the battery eliminator?

qAndA.answer: The ammeter has magnets inside which can affect the magnetic needle of the Tangent Galvanometer.
qAndA.question: Why should the ammeter be placed away from the Tangent Galvanometer?

qAndA.answer: The ammeter reading is approximately 1.5 amperes.
qAndA.question: What is the reading on the ammeter after the experimenter adjusts the rheostat?

activities.description: The experimenter writes on a white paper using a red pen. The text on the paper describes the goal of the experiment: to measure the horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field using a Tangent Galvanometer.
The experimenter presents the equipment necessary for the experiment: a tangent galvanometer, a battery eliminator, a commutator, a variable resistance (rheostat), an ammeter, and connecting wires.

The experimenter explains the connections required for the experiment: positive terminal of battery connected to the commutator, negative to the rheostat, top end of rheostat to ammeter, bottom end to battery negative, and the other two terminals to the tangent galvanometer.
The experimenter explains that the ammeter carries magnets within and should not be placed close to the tangent galvanometer.
The experimenter explains that the coil of the tangent galvanometer should be placed parallel to the magnetic needle.
The experimenter places the coil parallel to the magnetic needle.
The experimenter ensures that a thin pointer coincides with the 0-0 position of the compass box in the tangent galvanometer.
The experimenter connects the wires to the mains.
The experimenter switches the power on.
The experimenter turns on the battery and sets the voltage to 8 volts.
The experimenter sets the commutator to the correct position.
The experimenter adjusts the rheostat to achieve a reading of 1.5 amperes on the ammeter.

climax.description: The experimenter adjusts the rheostat to achieve a reading of 1.5 amperes on the ammeter.
